Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 12, verses 1–3:

Explanation of the words:

Alif-Lam-Ra (ألر): It is written alif-lam-ra and read "Alif, Lam, Ra." Allah knows best what He means by it.

The Clear Book (الكتاب المبين): That is, the Qur'an, which makes the truth manifest in matters of belief, worship and legislation.

An Arabic Qur'an (قرآنا عربيا): That is, revealed in a language that the 'Adnanite and Qahtanite Arabs alike could understand.

We relate to you (نحن نقص): We narrate to you, following the traces of the narrative in the manner in which it occurred and was accomplished.

By what We have revealed to you (بما أوحينا): That is, by Our revelation to you; revelation is the means of relating stories.

Before it (من قبله): That is, before its descent upon you.

Among the unaware (لمن الغافلين): That is, before Our revelation to you you were unaware of it; you did not mention it and knew nothing of it.

Meaning of the verses:

The connection between Surah Hud and Surah Yusuf, peace be upon them, is that the second completes the narrative contained in the first. Surah Yusuf contains the longest narrative in the Noble Qur'an. It begins with ﴿When Yusuf said to his father﴾ [Verse: 4], the fourth verse, and ends with ﴿And you were not with them when they resolved on their plan while they were conspiring﴾ [Verse: 102], the hundred and second verse. As for the occasion of revelation of this surah, it is said that the Messenger ﷺ was told: "If only you would relate to us," and Allah the Exalted revealed ﴿Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the verses of the Clear Book﴾ up to His words ﴿And you were not with them when they resolved on their plan while they were conspiring﴾ [Verse: 102]. So it relates events of roughly forty years. His words "Alif, Lam, Ra" are among the disjointed letters from which the verses of the Noble Qur'an were composed; He refers to them with His words ﴿These are the verses of the Clear Book﴾, that is, the one that makes the truth clear and manifest, and everything that people need that would set right their religion and their worldly affairs. His words ﴿Indeed, We have sent it down﴾, that is, the Qur'an, ﴿as an Arabic Qur'an﴾, that is, in the tongue of the Arabs, so that they might understand it, comprehend its meanings, be guided by it, and thus be perfected and made happy. His words ﴿so that you might reason﴾, that is, so that you may be able to understand it and recognize the guidance and light that it contains. His words ﴿We relate to you﴾, O Messenger of Allah, ﴿the best of stories﴾, that is, the most sound, truthful, beneficial and beautiful of them, ﴿by what We have revealed to you of this Qur'an﴾, that is, through Our revelation to you of this Qur'an, ﴿and indeed you were before it﴾, that is, before its revelation to you, ﴿among the unaware﴾ of it, not mentioning it and not knowing it.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Affirmation of the inimitability of the Qur'an, for it is composed of letters like Alif-Lam-Ra, Ta-Sin, and Qaf, yet the Arabs were unable to produce a surah like it.

2- Explanation of the wisdom in the revelation of the Qur'an in the Arabic language, which is that the Arabs might understand it and convey it to others.

3- The Noble Qur'an contains the best of narratives, so there is no point in listening to the stories of others.

4- Affirmation of the prophethood of the Messenger ﷺ and its establishment by the strongest rational proof and the greatest transmitted evidence.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 12, verses 4–6:

Explanation of the words:

*li-abihi* (to his father): that is Ya'qub (Jacob), son of Ishaq (Isaac), son of Ibrahim (Abraham), the Friend (al-Khalil), peace be upon him.

*inni ra'aytu* (indeed I saw): that is, in my dream.

*ahada 'ashara kawkaban* (eleven stars): that is, from the stars of the sky.

*sajidin* (prostrating): that is, all of them descended from the sky and prostrated to Yusuf while he was a child.

*fayakidu laka* (so they will plot against you): that is, they will scheme against you with that which harms you.

*'aduwwun mubin* (a manifest enemy): that is, clearly hostile in its apparent form.

*yajtabika rabbuka* (your Lord will choose you): that is, He will select you for Himself, so that you may be among His sincere servants.

*min ta'wil al-ahadith* (of the interpretation of narrations): that is, the interpretation of dreams.

*wa yutimmu ni'matahu 'alayka* (and complete His favour upon you): that is, by giving you prophethood and sending you as a messenger.

The meaning of the verses:

His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿When Yusuf said﴾: this is the beginning of the narrative. That is, remember, O Messenger, when Yusuf son of Ya'qub said to his father Ya'qub ﴿O my father﴾, that is, O my father, ﴿indeed I saw eleven stars﴾, that is, from the stars of the sky, ﴿and the sun and the moon—I saw them prostrating to me﴾, that is, they descended from the sky and prostrated to him in greeting and honour. The interpretation of this dream will become manifest after forty years, when Allah reunites his family with his two parents and his eleven brothers, and they all prostrate to him in greeting and honour. And His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿He said: O my son﴾, that is, Ya'qub said to his son Yusuf, ﴿do not relate your dream to your brothers﴾, and they are his brothers from his father but not from his mother, ﴿lest they devise a plot against you﴾, that is, envy will move them to scheme against you with that which harms you, by obeying Satan when he incites them against you. ﴿Indeed, Satan is to man a manifest enemy﴾, for he expelled Adam and Eve from the Garden by adorning for them eating from the tree from which Allah, may He be exalted, had forbidden them to eat. And His saying ﴿And thus will your Lord choose you﴾: and just as your Lord showed you the stars, the sun and the moon prostrating to you, He will choose you, that is, select you for Himself, so that you may be among His sincere servants.

And His saying ﴿and teach you the interpretation of narrations﴾, that is, and He will teach you knowledge of what the narrations and dreams of people will lead to, ﴿and complete His favour upon you and upon the family of Ya'qub﴾, that is, his children, by prophethood. ﴿Just as He completed it upon your two fathers before, Ibrahim and Ishaq﴾: Ishaq was Yusuf's nearer grandfather and Ibrahim his greater grandfather, upon whom He bestowed great favours, the greatest of which were prophethood and messengership. And His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿Indeed your Lord is Knowing﴾, that is, of His creation, ﴿Wise﴾, that is, in His management, placing each thing in its proper place, honouring the one who deserves honour and denying the one who deserves deprivation.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The validity of dreams in the Law and the legitimacy of interpreting them.

2- A dream may be delayed, so that its fulfilment does not appear until many years later.

3- The legitimacy of caution and taking precautions in important matters.

4- Clarification of Allah's bounty upon the family of Ibrahim, by which He made them prophets, fathers, sons and grandsons.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 12, verses 7–10:

Explanation of the words:

Āyāt lil-sā'ilīn (signs for those who ask): lessons for those who inquire about their news and the strange circumstances they went through.

Naḥnu 'uṣbah (we are a band): that is, a group, for they were eleven men.

Aw iṭrāḥūhu arḍan (or cast him onto some land): that is, throw him into a distant land where he will not be found.

Yakhlu lakum wajhu abīkum (the face of your father will be free for you): that is, from gazing at Yusuf, so that he will turn to you and not look to anyone else.

Fī ghayābat al-jubb (in the depths of the well): that is, the darkness of the well.

Ba'ḍ al-sayyārah (some of the caravan): that is, the travelers journeying across the land.

The meaning of the verses:

The context still concerns the story of Yusuf, peace be upon him. Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Certainly there were in Yusuf and his brothers signs for those who ask﴾, that is, in the matter of Yusuf and his brothers and what befell them and the great events that took place, there are lessons and admonitions for those who ask about that and seek to know it. ﴿When they said﴾, that is, the brothers of Yusuf, ﴿"Yusuf and his brother are dearer to our father than we, though we are a band"﴾, that is, a group. How then does he prefer the two over the group? ﴿Indeed our father is in manifest error﴾, that is, in clear mistake by giving preference to Yusuf and his brother in love over us. As for His saying: ﴿"Kill Yusuf or cast him onto some land, so the face of your father will be free for you"﴾, Allah, the Exalted, informs of what the brothers of Yusuf said while they were in private, conspiring against their brother to be rid of him. They said: ﴿"Kill Yusuf"﴾ by taking his life, ﴿"or cast him onto some land"﴾ in a distant place where you throw him so that he perishes, and you will be rid of him without killing him yourselves. Thereby ﴿the face of your father will be free for you﴾, since he was occupied with looking at Yusuf, and he will love you and you will love him, and you will repent to Allah for the sin of removing Yusuf from his father, and you will be after that righteous people, since nothing will remain that burdens you with sin or earns you wrongdoing. As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿A speaker among them said﴾, Allah, the Exalted, informs of the words of the brothers of Yusuf to one another while they consulted about the matter of Yusuf and how to keep him away from their father and his approval of them. A speaker among them said, he was Yahuda or Ruben, and he was their brother and maternal cousin, and he was the oldest of them in age and the soundest in judgment. He said: "Do not kill Yusuf, for killing is a crime that cannot be borne and must not be committed under any circumstances, but cast him into the depths of the well," that is, the darkness of the well, a well well known in their lands in the land of Palestine, "some of the caravan will pick him up, if you are going to do something concerning your brother." This is the best way to do that.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- Inclining toward one of the children with love produces enmity among brothers.

2- Envy is the cause of many human calamities.

3- Choosing the lesser of two harms is a legal principle that the early generations acted upon.

4- Compassion and love for a full brother is greater than that for a half-brother.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 12, Verses 11–14**

**Explanation of the words:**

*Lanasihun* (لناصحون): We are truly concerned for him, wishing him all good as we wish it for ourselves.

*Yarta'* *wa-yal'ab* (يرتع ويلعب): He eats, drinks and plays, by racing and wrestling.

*Inni la-yahzununi* (إني ليحزنني): It causes me to fall into grief, which is pain of the soul, namely your taking him away.

*Al-dhi'b* (الذئب): A predatory, deceitful and fierce animal.

*Wa-nahnu 'usbah* (ونحن عصبة): A strong group.

*La-khasirun* (لخاسرون): Weak and powerless, exposed to loss by our losing our brother.

**The meaning of the verses:**

The context still concerns the story of Joseph. After they had conspired and secretly agreed to throw Joseph into the depths of the well (*ghayabat al-jubb*), they asked their father to let Joseph go out with them to the open country, as was their custom, for an outing and recreation. They sensed that their father did not trust them, so they said to him: ﴿What is the matter with you that you do not entrust us with Joseph, when we are indeed sincere toward him?﴾, meaning: we wish him every good and are concerned that no harm should touch him. ﴿Send him with us tomorrow to frolic and play﴾, meaning: he will graze in the countryside, eat fruit, drink milk and eat meat, and play with what we play, such as racing, wrestling and fighting. ﴿And indeed we will be his guardians﴾ from everything that might harm him or cause him injury.

He, peace be upon him, answered them, saying: ﴿Indeed, it saddens me that you take him away﴾, meaning: your taking him away would cause me to fall into grief and its pain. ﴿And I fear that the wolf will devour him while you are heedless of him﴾, meaning: heedless in your grazing and play.

They answered him, saying: ﴿If the wolf devours him while we are a group, then indeed we would be losers﴾, meaning: there is no good in our existence if we are overpowered over our brother and the wolf devours him in our midst.

Sadly, his father was persuaded by this speech, and tomorrow they would take Joseph away to carry out their base plot.

**Guidance from the verses:**

1. Establishing the principle: there is no caution against decree, meaning no precaution benefits in turning away what has been decreed.

2. The truthfulness of the believer leads him to accept the oath of one who swears to him and confirms his words.

3. Grief is permissible and carries no sin. In the hadith: "Indeed we, O Ibrahim, are saddened by your separation."

4. If a person is heedless, the wolf's devouring of a human being does occur, and it is frequent as well.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 12, verses 15–18:

Explanation of the words:

Wa-ajma'u (and they resolved): that is, they agreed upon their plan to cast him into the depths of the well.

Fi ghayabat al-jubb (into the darkness of the well): that is, into the darkness at the bottom of the well.

Wa-awhayna ilayhi (and We revealed to him): that is, We informed him by a hidden and swift means.

Ishā' (nightfall): that is, after the sun has set, at the beginning of the night.

Nastabiq (we went racing): that is, competing in running.

ʿind matā'inā (by our belongings): that is, our goods, such as clothes and other things.

Wa-mā anta bi-mu'minin lanā (and you will not believe us): that is, you will not accept us as truthful.

Bi-dam kadhib (with false blood): that is, with blood that is falsified, meaning the blood of a young goat and not the blood of Yusuf.

Bal sawwalat lakum (rather, your souls have embellished for you): that is, adorned and made attractive.

ʿAlā mā taṣifūn (concerning what you describe): that is, of falsehood.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues to report what the brothers of Yusuf resolved to do. They had persuaded their father the previous day to send Yusuf with them to the open country, and here they are, having taken him with them and gone out with him. As soon as they were far away, their faces changed toward him, and he began to receive abusive words, shoving, and at times beating. They had resolved to cast him into a well known to them in the desert, and they carried out their scheme and threw their brother down while he was crying at the top of his voice; they had stripped off his shirt and left him bound in the bottom of the well. At this point God the Exalted revealed to him, that is, informed him by whatever means of knowledge He willed, that he would surely inform them one day of this their shameful deed. This is the meaning of His words in the context: ﴿And We revealed to him: you will surely inform them of this matter of theirs, while they do not perceive﴾. After they had finished with their brother, they slaughtered a young goat and smeared its blood on his shirt, and returned to their father in the evening, weeping, bearing the calamity to their father, the aged old man. God the Exalted said: ﴿And they came to their father in the evening﴾, that is, at night, ﴿weeping﴾, and they said, making excuses: ﴿O our father, we went racing against one another and left Yusuf by our belongings, and the wolf devoured him. But you will not believe us, even if we are truthful﴾, that is, you will not accept us as truthful. Their statements showed their lying. God the Exalted said: ﴿And they came with false blood upon his shirt﴾, that is, blood that is a lie or falsified, since it was the blood of a young goat which they slaughtered and ate, and they smeared some of its blood on the shirt of Yusuf, their brother. Yaʿqub looked at the shirt, smeared with the false blood, and there was no tear or rent in it, so he said: "Indeed, this wolf is gentle, since it devoured Yusuf yet did not tear his garment." Then he said what God the Exalted reported in His words: ﴿He said: rather, your souls have embellished a matter for you﴾, that is, the matter was not as you described and claimed, but your souls adorned for you a matter and you carried it out. ﴿So patience is beautiful﴾, that is, my affair is patience, complete. Beautiful patience is that in which there is no impatience and no complaint. ﴿And God is the One whose help is sought against what you describe﴾, that is, against the lying.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The permissibility of a great sin proceeding from a believing man who is being prepared for perfection in the future.

2- God's kindness toward Yusuf and His honoring him by informing him that he would surely inform his brothers of this deed, and in that He gave him the good news of well-being of condition and a good outcome.

3- The choice of night for making excuses rather than day, because the eye is shy before the eye, as it is said. And as it was said: "How can one hope for shame from a friend... when the place of shame from him is ruined," meaning, his two eyes do not see.

4- The virtue of beautiful patience, which is free of both impatience and complaint.

Explanation of the words:

Waridahum (their water-bearer): i.e., the one who comes to them to draw water.

Fa-adla dalwahu (so he let down his bucket): i.e., he lowered his bucket into the well.

Wa-asarruhu bidaa'ah (and they concealed him as merchandise): i.e., they hid him as one hides a commodity.

Wa-shaaruhu bithaman bakhs (and they sold him for a meager price): i.e., they sold him for a deficient price.

Wa-qala alladhi ishtarahu (and the one who bought him said): i.e., the man who bought him, whose name was Qitfir and whose title was al-'Aziz (the Minister).

Akrimi mathwahu (make his residence honorable): i.e., make honorable the place where he stays, meaning honor him and treat him well.

Aw nattakhidhahu waladan (or we may adopt him as a son): i.e., we may adopt him; he said this because he had no children.

Min ta'wil al-ahadith (the interpretation of narrations): i.e., the interpretation of dreams.

Hukman wa-'ilman (wisdom and knowledge): i.e., wisdom in management and knowledge in religion.

The noble context continues to speak of Yusuf and his brothers. When Yusuf was thrown into the well and left there, a caravan came from the land of Madyan heading to Egypt. They sent their water-bearer to draw water for them, and he let down his bucket into the well, and Yusuf clung to it, and he came out with him. This is what is indicated by the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And a caravan came, and they sent their water-bearer, and he let down his bucket. He said, "What good news! This is a boy!" His words, ﴿and that We may teach him the interpretation of narrations﴾, i.e., that We may teach him the interpretation of dreams from the talk of people and what they relate of them. In this is good tidings to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ of a good outcome, and that Allah, the Exalted, will grant him victory over his enemies and establish him over them.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Permissibility of rejoicing at what pleases and announcing it.

2- Permissibility of taking precaution for matters of religion and worldly life.

3- The word "purchase" (shira') is applied to sale.

4- Abrogation of adoption (tabanni) in Islam.

5- Knowing the interpretation of dreams is a gift of honor to whom Allah has taught it.

6- Whoever overcomes Allah is overcome.

7- The attainment of maturity (bulugh al-ashudd) begins with the end of childhood and entry into puberty.

8- Good reward is conditional upon good intention and action.

Raawadat (she sought to seduce): i.e., she asked him for her desire, wanting him to lower his will to her will, but he refused.

Allati huwa fi baytiha (she in whose house he was): i.e., Zulaykha, the wife of al-'Aziz.

Waghallaqat al-abwab (and she locked the doors): she closed them with bolts.

Hayta laka (come, I am ready for you): i.e., come to me.

Ma'adh Allah (God forbid): i.e., I seek refuge in God, I shelter and protect myself with Him from doing what is not permitted.

Ahsana mathwaya (he has treated me well in his home): i.e., my residence in his house.

Hammat bihi (she resolved upon him): i.e., she intended to strike him violently.

Wahamma biha (and he resolved toward her): i.e., he intended to repel her assault upon him.

Burhan Rabbih (the proof of his Lord): his Lord inspired him that the good lay in not striking her.

Al-su' wal-fahsha' (evil and indecency): al-su' is what would cause harm, namely striking her; al-fahsha' is the ugly trait.

Al-mukhlisin (the sincere ones): i.e., those whom We have chosen for Our guardianship, obedience and love.

Waqadat qamisahu (she tore his shirt): i.e., she cut it from behind.

Wa alfaya sayyidaha (and they found her husband): i.e., they found al-'Aziz, her husband; they used the word sayyid (master) for the husband because he owns the wife.

The meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues to speak of Yusuf and the events that befell him in the house of al-'Aziz, who had bought him. As soon as al-'Aziz instructed his wife to honor Yusuf, she hastened to do so, making his food, drink, clothing and bedding good. Given that seclusion between a man and a woman stirs sexual desire, especially when the period is long, and fear dissolves and piety diminishes, she actually sought to seduce him, that is, her self asked him to lie with her, after she had taken the enabling means: she locked the doors of the chamber, the hall and the courtyard, and said, "Come to me." Yusuf's response to her request was firm and decisive, cutting off greed, and this is what is required in such a situation. God the Exalted says, reporting what happened in the palace, where no one among people knows what took place and what events occurred there:

﴿And she in whose house he was sought to seduce him, and she locked the doors and said, "Come, you." He said, "God forbid! Indeed, he is my lord; he has made my residence excellent. Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed."﴾ After she had taken every necessary measure to obtain her desire from him, he answered her saying: ﴿Indeed, he is my lord; he has made my residence excellent﴾, meaning: al-'Aziz has made my residence good, so how could I betray him regarding his family? At the same time, his true Master, God the Majestic, has made his residence good by subjecting things for him, so how could he betray Him in what He has forbidden to him? His saying "Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed" is a second reason: the wrongdoer, by placing a thing in other than its place, fails in his endeavor and loses in this world and the next. So how could I be content for myself and for you with that?

God's saying: ﴿And she certainly desired him, and he would have desired her had he not seen the proof of his Lord﴾ means: she resolved to strike him, because he refused her request after solicitations that had lasted a long time; and he resolved toward her, that is, to strike her, to repel her from himself. But God showed him a proof within himself, so he did not strike her, and he preferred to flee outside the house. She ran after him to bring him back, out of fear that someone would learn what she had done with him. ﴿And they raced to the door﴾: he wanted to go out while she wanted to return him to the house out of fear of disgrace, and she seized him by his shirt and tore it from behind, because he was in front of her and she was behind him.

God's saying: ﴿Thus, that We might avert from him evil and indecency﴾ means: thus do We avert from Yusuf evil, so that he does not commit it, and indecency, so that he does not approach it. He gives the reason for that by saying: ﴿Indeed, he is of Our sincere servants﴾, that is, those whom We have chosen for Our worship and love, so We do not allow them to be stained by the traces of sins and disobedience. God's saying: ﴿And they found her husband at the door﴾ means: they found her husband sitting at the door in the state of his fleeing from her, while she ran after him until they reached the door, and behold, al-'Aziz was sitting there. She feared disgrace for herself, so she hastened to excuse herself, saying: "What is the recompense for one who intended evil to your family, except that he be imprisoned, that is, for a day or two, or a painful punishment as his recompense, such as being severely beaten?"

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 12, verses 26–29:

Explanation of the words:

"And a witness from her family testified": i.e., her paternal cousin.

"If his shirt is torn from the front": i.e., from in front.

"And if his shirt is torn from the back": i.e., from behind, from the rear.

"Indeed, it is of your guile": i.e., her statement, "What is the recompense for one who intended evil to your family..."

"Joseph, turn away from this": i.e., from this matter, and do not mention it, lest it spread.

"Of those who err": those who commit sins, the sinful.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues to speak of Joseph and the events of the story. Zulaykha claimed that Joseph had sought to seduce her and demanded his punishment, saying, ﴿What is the recompense for one who intended evil to your family, except that he be imprisoned or suffer a painful punishment?﴾ [Yusuf: 25]. Here Joseph responded to what she had accused him of. Had she not accused him, he would not have reported her solicitation of him, so he said what God, the Exalted, reports in these verses: ﴿She sought to seduce me from myself.﴾ Here God, majestic in His majesty, caused an infant at the breast to speak, out of honor for His servant and chosen one, Joseph, and this infant, whom the Messenger of God (ﷺ) named "the witness of Joseph," said: ﴿If his shirt is torn from the front, then she has spoken truly, and he is of the liars. But if his shirt is torn from the back, then she has lied, and he is of the truthful.﴾ This is the judgment of the young witness.

﴿So when he saw his shirt torn from the back, he said﴾ — ﴿Indeed, it is of your guile﴾, i.e., her statement, ﴿"What is the recompense for one who intended evil to your family..."﴾ [Yusuf: 25], ﴿of the guile of you women﴾, i.e., of the doings of women: ﴿Indeed, your guile is great.﴾ Then he said to Joseph, "O Joseph, turn away from this," i.e., from this matter, and do not mention it to anyone, lest it spread and cause harm. And he said to Zulaykha, ﴿And ask forgiveness for your sin﴾, i.e., seek pardon from your husband, that he may overlook it and not hold you accountable for the sin you committed, ﴿for indeed you were of those who erred﴾, i.e., of the sinful among the people. This is what these four verses contain in this noble context.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The legitimacy of defending oneself, even with what may offend the opponent.

2- God's honoring of His friends, in that He made an infant in the cradle speak and thus judged Joseph's innocence.

3- Affirmation that the guile of women is great, and it is so.

4- The recommendation of concealing the faults of the one who errs, and the disapproval of spreading sins among people.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 12, verses 30–34:

Explanation of the words:

Fi al-madina (in the city): that is, the capital of Egypt at that time.

Turawidu fatahā (she seeks to seduce her young man): that is, her slave, the Canaanite.

Qad shaghafaha hubban (her love for him has pierced her): that is, his love entered the shaghaf (the inner covering) of her heart, meaning it surrounded her heart and took possession of it.

Inna lanarahā fī dalālin mubīn (indeed we see her in manifest error): that is, in clear mistake because of her love for him.

Falammā samiʿat bi-makrihinna (when she heard of their scheming): that is, of what they said about her in her absence.

Wa-aʿtadat lahunna muttaka'an (and she prepared for them a reclining place): that is, she prepared for them cushions and pillows to recline upon.

Akbarnahu (they magnified him in their souls): that is, they held him in great esteem in their hearts.

Fa-dhālikunna alladhī lumtunnanī fīh (this is the one about whom you blamed me): that is, you said, how can she love a Canaanite slave?

Fa-istaʿṣama (so he held firmly to chastity): that is, he refrained, holding fast to his purity and virtue.

Al-ṣāghirīn (the abased): the humiliated and degraded.

Aṣbu ilayhinna (I would incline toward them): that is, I would be inclined toward them.

Wa-akun min al-jāhilīn (and I would be among the ignorant): that is, among the sinners, since no one sins except one who is ignorant of God's power and His watchfulness over him.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues with the story of Yusuf. After the judgment issued by the witness, which was Yusuf, peace be upon him, the news spread to the wives of some ministers. They gathered in the house of one of them and spoke in a manner that blamed the wife of the al-ʿAzīz, who had sought to seduce her slave, the Canaanite, against his will. This is what God, exalted is He, reported in the following verses. God says: ﴿And the women in the city said, "The wife of the al-ʿAzīz is seeking to seduce her young man from himself. He has captivated her heart with love; indeed, we see her in manifest error."﴾ That is, the capital of Egypt at that time. ﴿The wife of the al-ʿAzīz is seeking to seduce her young man﴾, that is, her slave. ﴿From himself; he has captivated her with love﴾, that is, her love for him has reached the shaghaf of her heart, meaning its covering. ﴿Indeed, we see her﴾, that is, we think her ﴿in manifest error﴾, that is, a clear mistake: how could she love a slave when she is who she is in her nobility and high station? God's words: ﴿So when she heard of their scheming﴾, that is, what they said about her in her absence, ﴿she sent for them and prepared for them a reclining place and gave each one of them a knife﴾. That is, she countered their scheming with a greater scheme. She prepared a banquet of food and drink. When they began to eat, cutting fruits with knives, such as citron and others, she ordered him to come out to them so they could see him. They would be amazed at the sight, become distracted from themselves, and cut their hands instead of the fruit they were cutting for food. Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 12, verses 39–42:

Explanation of the words:

"O my two companions in the prison" (يا صاحبي السجن): i.e., O my two companions in the prison, who were the two young men, the king's cup-bearer and the king's baker.

"Are lords dispersed better, or Allah, the One, the Subduer?" (أأرباب متفرقون): i.e., gods dispersed here and there, meaning in their essences, their attributes and their places.

"Besides Him" (من دونه): i.e., besides Allah, glorified and exalted be He.

"Except names" (إلا أسماء): i.e., merely the name of a god; in reality it is not a god but an idol.

"For which Allah has sent down no authority" (ما أنزل الله بها من سلطان): i.e., Allah has not commanded that they be worshipped in any form of worship.

"He will give his lord wine to drink" (فيسقي ربه خمرا): i.e., he will give his master, who is the king of the land, wine to drink.

"He will be crucified" (فيصلب): i.e., he will be killed by being crucified on a wooden post, as was their customary way of execution.

"The matter has been decided" (قضي الأمر): i.e., it has been completed and settled.

"He thought that he would be saved of the two" (ظن أنه ناج منهما): i.e., he was certain that he would be declared innocent.

"Mention me to your lord" (أذكرني عند ربك): i.e., mention me to the king, that I am imprisoned unjustly, without any crime.

"So Satan caused him to forget the remembrance of his lord" (فأنساه الشيطان ذكر ربه): i.e., Satan caused Joseph to forget the remembrance of his Lord, exalted be He.

Explanation of the verses:

The noble context continues to speak of Joseph while he is in prison. The two young men had earlier asked him to interpret their dreams, that is, they asked him to interpret them for them, because they knew he interprets dreams. Joseph, however, took the opportunity and began to tell them about the reasons for his knowledge of the interpretation of dreams, and that he had abandoned the creed of disbelief and believed in Allah alone, and that in this he follows the creed of his fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and that it is not fitting for them to associate anything with Allah. In this there was an allusion to the polytheism of the people of the prison, in worshipping idols. He continued his speech, calling to Allah, the Exalted, and said what Allah, the Exalted, has reported in this context: "O my two companions in the prison, are lords dispersed better, or Allah, the One, the Subduer?" So he addressed his two companions: "O my two companions in the prison, tell me and be truthful: are lords, meaning gods dispersed here and there? This is an idol, this is a star, this is a human, this is an animal, this one has such a color and that one has such a color. Is that better, or Allah, the One in His essence and attributes, the Subduer over everything other than Him among all created beings?" They had no answer other than "Allah, the One, the Subduer," for reason requires this. Then he addressed the people of the prison as a whole and said: "What you worship besides Him" (ما تعبدون من دونه), i.e., besides Allah, the One, the Subduer, "are only names that you and your fathers have named" (إلا أسماء سميتموها أنتم وآباؤكم). They are merely names and nothing more; for your calling an idol or a star, to which a form has been drawn, "god" or "lord" does not make it a lord and a god. The Lord is the Creator, the Provider, the Manager; but a created thing that is provided for and that possesses no power to benefit or harm itself, let alone others, to call it lord and god is a lie and a falsehood. They are names "for which Allah has sent down no authority," no proof or evidence, so that they should be worshipped on the basis that Allah has commanded their worship. Then he said to them: "Judgment belongs only to Allah" (إن الحكم إلا لله), i.e., judgment belongs only to Allah, and He has judged that He alone is to be worshipped. Therefore every worship directed to other than Him is void and must be abandoned and renounced. "That is the upright religion" (ذلك الدين القيم): he informed them that worshipping Allah alone and abandoning the worship of others is the upright religion and the straight path. "But most people do not know": their ignorance of knowing their true Lord, who created them, provides for them, manages their lives, and to whom they will return, is what has caused them to worship what they carve and to deify what they make.

When he had finished calling to his Lord, he turned to the two who had asked him to interpret their dreams and said, as Allah, exalted be He, reported of him: "O my two companions in the prison, as for one of you, he will give his lord wine to drink" (أما أحدكما فيسقي ربه خمرا), i.e., he will be released and return to his work with the king, and give him wine to drink as he used to give him before. "As for the other, he will be crucified and the birds will eat from his head after his crucifixion." The other was the king's baker, who was accused of intending to put poison in the king's food to kill him. Then the two said: "We have not seen anything; we only asked you to test you, nothing more." He answered them: "The matter about which you inquire has been decided" (قضي الأمر الذي فيه تستفتيان), i.e., it has been completed and settled, whether you saw it or did not see it. Then he said to the one who thought he would be saved of the two, as Allah, exalted be He, reported: "Mention me to your lord" (اذكرني عند ربك), i.e., to your master; they used to call the master and owner "lord." "So Satan caused him to forget the remembrance of his lord": i.e., Satan caused Joseph, peace be upon him, to forget the remembrance of his Lord, exalted be He, when his heart turned to the servant and the king and he forgot Allah, so his true Lord punished him, and he remained in prison "for several years," i.e., seven years, by count.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The obligation to seize opportunities to call to Allah, the Exalted.

2- Establishing monotheism through the accounts of earlier people.

3- There is no judgment in anything except the judgment of Allah, the Exalted. The truth is what Allah makes true, falsehood is what He makes void, and religion is what He has legislated.

4- The legitimacy of seeking a ruling (istifta') in every difficult matter.

5- The heedlessness of Joseph, peace be upon him, in turning to the young man and saying to him, "Mention me to your lord," forgetting his true Master and Protector who saved him from being killed and from the depths of the well; and the trial of women caused him to be imprisoned for seven years.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 12, verses 43–46:

Explanation of the words:

al-Malik (the King): the king of Egypt, whose minister was al-Aziz, one of his ministers; his name was al-Rayyan ibn al-Walid.

Sab' 'ijaf (seven lean ones): emaciated, not plump.

Ya ayyuha al-mala' (O chiefs): O notables and dignitaries among the men of the state.

Aftuni fi ru'ya'i (explain to me my vision): i.e., interpret it for me.

Adghath ahlam (confused dreams): i.e., a jumble of false dreams that have no interpretation other than that.

Wadhdhakara ba'da ummah (and he remembered after a period): i.e., and he recalled after a time, namely about seven years.

Yusuf ayyuha as-siddiq (Joseph, O truthful one): i.e., O Joseph, O one who is very truthful, a quality known of him in prison.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues to speak of Joseph in his trial. When the time of his relief drew near, the King of Egypt saw a vision that disturbed him, and he asked the men of his state to interpret it. This is what Allah, the Exalted, informs of in these verses, when He says, ﴿And the King said, "Indeed, I see seven fat cows being eaten by seven lean ones"﴾, meaning, emaciated in the utmost leanness. ﴿And seven green spikes and others dry﴾, meaning, dry ears of grain. Then he confronted the men of knowledge and state around him, whom he had gathered for this purpose, and said, ﴿O chiefs, explain to me my vision, if you are able to interpret visions﴾, meaning, to explain them.

They answered him, as Allah informs of them in His saying, ﴿They said, "Confused dreams"﴾, meaning, your vision is one of confused dreams that cannot be interpreted, for they said, ﴿And we are not learned in the interpretation of dreams﴾. What is meant by adghath is jumbles. In the authentic hadith: "The good dream is from the Most Merciful, and the bad dream is from Satan."

And His saying, ﴿And the one who was saved of the two said﴾, meaning, of the two companions of the prison, ﴿and remembered after a time﴾, meaning, he recalled what Joseph had instructed him when he was bidding him farewell at the prison door, when he said to him, ﴿Mention me to your lord﴾ [Yusuf: 42], after a period of time, about seven years. He said what Allah informs of him: ﴿I will inform you of its interpretation, so send me forth﴾, meaning, to Joseph in prison, for he is the best of those who interpret dreams. So they sent him, and he came to him and said what Allah informs of him in His saying, ﴿"Joseph, O truthful one, explain to us about seven fat cows being eaten by seven lean ones, and seven green spikes and others dry"﴾. And His saying, ﴿that I may return to the people﴾, meaning, the king and his men, ﴿that they may know﴾, meaning, what you interpret it as, so that they may benefit from that.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The permissibility of a good dream being seen by a disbeliever or a sinner.

2- Dreams are of two kinds: a dream from Satan, and a vision from the Most Merciful.

3- Forgetfulness is one of the attributes of humans.

4- The permissibility of describing a person by what is in him without flattery, as in his saying, "O truthful one."

5- La'alla (perhaps) can be used in the sense of kay (in order that) indicating purpose.

2- Dreams are of two kinds: a dream from Satan, and a vision from the Most Merciful.

3- Forgetfulness is one of the attributes of humans.

4- The permissibility of describing a person by what is in him without flattery, as in his saying, "O truthful one."

5- La'alla (perhaps) can be used in the sense of kay (in order that) indicating purpose.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 12, verses 47–49:

Explanation of the words:

Da'aban (dassociation, cultivation): meaning consecutively, as is your custom.

Fa-dharuhu fi sunbulihi: meaning leave it in its ear (sunbul) and do not thresh it.

Sab' shidad: meaning harsh, hard years because of the dryness (jadb) in them.

Bima tuhsinun: meaning you guard it and store it for seed and need.

Yughathu an-nas: meaning their Lord will give them relief with rain and the flowing of the Nile.

Wa-fihi ya'sirun: meaning that which is of the nature of being pressed, such as olives, grapes and sugar cane.

Meaning of the verses:

The words of the Exalted, ﴿He said: You shall sow﴾ and to the end, are Yusuf's reply to the one who consulted him, that is, who asked him to interpret the king's dream. He said to him, in explaining the interpretation of the dream: "You shall sow" means "sow," for seven years consecutively, as is your custom in planting each year, and this is the interpretation of the seven fat cows. "So what you reap of crops, leave it in its ear," that is, leave it without threshing so that it does not spoil, "except a little of what you eat," that is, thresh it for that purpose. "Then after that there will come" after the fruitful years "seven hard years," that is, harsh barren years, and this is the interpretation of the seven lean cows, "which will consume what you have stored for them," that is, of the grains you have kept from the seven fruitful years, meaning that you will eat it in them, "except a little of what you store," that is, what you keep for seed and the like. "Then after that there will come a year in which people will be given relief and in which they will press," that is, after the seven barren years there will come a year in which people will be given relief with rain and in which they will press grapes, oil and everything that is pressed, due to the presence of fertility in it.

As for His saying, "Then there will come after that a year," etc.: the dream did not indicate this; rather it is something Allah the Exalted taught Yusuf, and he informed them of it beyond what they had asked, out of kindness from him and for a lofty wisdom that Allah the Exalted intended. And He is the All-Wise, the All-Knowing.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- The land of Egypt is a land of farming and agriculture from its earliest era.

2- Storing the surplus in granaries and elsewhere is an important and beneficial economic principle.

3- Yusuf's excellence in interpreting dreams is a great thing.

4- The virtue of Yusuf, peace be upon him, over the people of Egypt, in that he informed them of more than they had asked.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 12, verses 50–52:

Explanation of the words:

"And the king said: Bring him to me": i.e., Yusuf.

"So when the messenger came to him": i.e., the messenger of the king.

"Return to your lord": i.e., your master.

"What is the case of the women": what is their condition.

"What was your affair": what was your matter.

"Hashа Lillah" (حاش لله, "Far be God from it"): i.e., glorifying God, exalted above being incapable of creating a chaste human being.

"Haṣḥaṣa al-ḥaqq" (حصحص الحق, "the truth became manifest"): the truth became clear and appeared.

Meaning of the verses:

The dream of the king was a arrangement from God Most High to bring Yusuf out of the prison. After the king saw the dream and his men were unable to interpret it, and one of the two companions of the prison remembered what Yusuf had enjoined upon him, the king asked that he be sent to Yusuf in the prison to seek his opinion regarding the dream. They sent him, he sought Yusuf's opinion, Yusuf gave him a ruling, and he took it to the king. The king was impressed by the interpretation and understood its meaning, and he ordered that Yusuf be brought to him to honor him, because of the knowledge and perfection that had become apparent to him. This is what God Most High reported in His saying: ﴿And the king said, "Bring him to me."﴾ i.e., Yusuf. ﴿So when the messenger came to him﴾ i.e., the king's messenger came to Yusuf, and he was his companion who had been with him in the prison and had been spared punishment and returned to serving the king. So he said to him: the king is calling you, and Yusuf said to him: go back to him and ask him ﴿what is the case of the women who cut their hands?﴾ i.e., tell him to ask about the condition of the women who cut their hands, and the woman who accused me. So the king gathered the women and asked them, saying: "What was your affair when you sought to seduce Yusuf from himself?" They answered: ﴿"Hashā lillāh! We know of no evil from him."﴾ i.e., we glorify God, exalted above being incapable of creating a chaste human being like this. ﴿We know of no evil from him.⁠﴾

And here the wife of the governor, Zulaykha, said what God Most High reported about her: ﴿"Now the truth has become manifest. I sought to seduce him from himself, and indeed he is of the truthful."⁠﴾ i.e., it became clear and manifest. ﴿"I sought to seduce him from himself"⁠﴾ and it was not he who sought me. And His saying, Most High: ﴿"That he may know that I did not betray him in secret"⁠﴾ is a report about Yusuf, peace be upon him, for he said that, i.e., my refusal to leave the prison and not answering the king, and my request that he ask about the condition of the women, until there was accomplished what was accomplished of my vindication through the tongues of the women in general and the wife of the governor in particular, for she definitively acknowledged my innocence and confirmed that it was she who sought to seduce me and I refused and rejected it. He did this so that her husband, the governor, would know that I did not betray him regarding his household in his absence, and that his honor is protected and his reputation was not defiled, because "He is my lord, who has made my residence good." ﴿And indeed God does not guide the scheme of the betrayers.⁠﴾ So had I been a betrayer, God would not have guided me to such a noble position, by which I became one whose innocence is established, whose honor is intact, and whose garment and ground are pure.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The virtue of knowledge and its nobility, for by it the king raised Yusuf to his presence, and he is exalted.

2- The virtue of forbearance and deliberation, and of not being hasty in matters.

3- The virtue of truthfulness and speaking the truth, even if it is against oneself.

4- The nobility of Zulaykha through her acknowledgment of her sin: it raised her to a lofty station and brought her to a high rank, for after a short while she would become the wife of God's chosen one, Yusuf the Truthful, son of the truthful, as a wife to him in this world and a wife to him in the Hereafter. This is the bounty of God, which He gives to whom He wills, and God is the possessor of great bounty.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 12, verses 53–57:

Explanation of the words:

*Li-ammaratun bil-su'* (لأمارة بالسوء): meaning, it frequently commands; "al-su'" (evil) is that which harms the human soul, such as sins.

*Illa ma rahima rabbi* (إلا ما رحم ربي): meaning, except for one whom my Lord has shown mercy; his soul does not command evil because of its goodness and purity.

*Astakhlisuhu li-nafsi* (استخلصه لنفسي): I will make him one of my intimates, among the people of my counsel and my secrets.

*Makin amin* (مكين أمين): meaning, one of standing by whom you are able to do whatever you wish; trustworthy, entrusted with everything we possess.

*Khaza'in al-ard* (خزائن الأرض): meaning, the treasuries of the state in the land of Egypt.

*Inni hafiz 'alim* (إني حفيظ عليم): meaning, I will safeguard what you entrust to me and preserve it, knowing how to manage it.

*Yatabawwa'* (يتبوأ): meaning, he will settle and dwell wherever he wishes, after having been in the depths of the well and the narrowness of the prison.

Explanation of the verses:

The discourse continues about Yusuf, peace be upon him. The words of the Exalted, ﴿And I do not absolve myself; indeed, the soul is incessantly commanding toward evil, except those upon which my Lord has mercy. Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, are the words of Yusuf, peace be upon him, when he said them after the king asked that the matter of the women who cut their hands and the wife of the ruler be investigated, and the investigation concluded with the declaration of Yusuf's innocence of what he had been accused of. He said this, meaning: it was done so that the ruler would know that I did not betray him in his absence, and that Allah does not guide the plotting of the treacherous. He also said it out of self-abasement on one hand, and on the other hand because he had intended to strike Zulaykha, as was mentioned earlier. He said: ﴿And I do not absolve myself﴾, and gave the reason for this, saying ﴿Indeed, the soul﴾, that is, the human soul, ﴿is incessantly commanding toward evil, except those upon which my Lord has mercy﴾, except a soul which my Lord has shown mercy to by guiding it to purify and cleanse itself through faith and righteous deeds, for it then becomes a tranquil soul that commands good and forbids evil. His words: ﴿Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ mention this sentence as a justification for his words ﴿And I do not absolve myself﴾; meaning, although there occurred from me an intention to strike, which is an evil, I have turned in repentance to Allah, and Allah is Forgiving, that is, He pardons and overlooks, so He does not hold accountable one who repents to Him, and He is Merciful to him, for He is Merciful to the believing among His servants. This is what the first verse [53] indicates.

As for the second verse [54] and the third [55], they contain the king's summoning of Yusuf and the conversation that took place between them, when the Exalted said: ﴿And the king said﴾, al-Rayyan ibn al-Walid, ﴿Bring him to me﴾, that is, Yusuf, after his knowledge and spiritual perfection had become manifest to him, ﴿that I may take him exclusively for myself﴾, that is, I will make him exclusively mine, consulting him in my affairs and seeking his help in the duties of my kingship. Yusuf came out of the prison, sat with the king, spoke with him, and asked him about the matter of the years of abundance and drought; he answered him with wise and sound measures that pleased his heart. Here the king said to him what the Exalted has reported: ﴿Indeed, you are today with us established and trusted﴾, that is, you hold a position with us that enables you to dispose of the land as you wish, and you are trusted with everything we possess. Yusuf answered him with what the Exalted has reported, saying: ﴿Appoint me over the treasuries of the land﴾, that is, the land of Egypt. The meaning of this is that he took the place of the ruler, who had died in those days.

He gave the reason for his request for the office of finance and economy by saying: ﴿Indeed, I am a knowing guardian﴾, that is, a guardian over what I am put in charge of, knowing how to administer and manage affairs. The Exalted's words in the fourth verse [56]: ﴿And thus We established Yusuf in the land, to settle therein wherever he willed﴾, that is, by means of such causes and measures We established Yusuf in the land of Egypt, to settle in it, that is, to descend wherever he wishes and move about in it, taking, giving, building, and developing, because he had become a minister with absolute authority. The Exalted's words: ﴿We bestow Our mercy upon whom We will﴾, that is, His mercy upon Our servants, ﴿and We do not waste the reward of the good-doers﴾. This is a promise from Allah the Exalted to the people of goodness that He will give them their full rewards. Yusuf, peace be upon him, is among those upon whom Allah has willed mercy, and he is among the people of goodness whose rewards Allah the Exalted gives in this world and the Hereafter. The Exalted has also informed us that the reward of the Hereafter is better for those who believe and were mindful of Allah, encouraging faith and godwariness, for through them one attains the guardianship of Allah the Exalted, since His friends are the believers who are mindful of Him.

Lessons of the verses:

From the lessons of the verses:

1- The virtue of humbling oneself by ascribing to oneself deficiency and shortcoming.

2- Confirmation of the saying: a person is hidden beneath his tongue.

3- Permissibility of a candidate for work mentioning his skill in the craft and the like, and this is not considered self-praise.

4- The virtue of goodness in belief, speech and action.

5- The excellence of faith and godwariness.

**Explanation of the words:**

*"And the brothers of Joseph came"*: from the land of Canaan, when news reached them that the king of Egypt was selling food.

*"And they were unknown to him"*: that is, they did not recognize that he was their brother.

*"And when he had furnished them with their provisions"*: that is, he honoured them and supplied them with what they needed for their journey, after he had measured out for them what they had bought from him.

*"With a brother of yours from your father"*: this is Benjamin, who had not come with them because their father could not bear to be parted from him.

*"We will seek to persuade his father concerning him"*: that is, we will strive earnestly to obtain him from him.

*"And he said to his servants"*: that is, his attendants and servants.

*"Their merchandise"*: that is, their silver coins with which they had come to buy grain.

**The meaning of the verses:**

The noble context continues the account of the story of Joseph (peace be upon him) and the tracing of its events. After Joseph was appointed to the office of minister and the years of plenty passed and the years of drought came, the people of the land of Canaan needed food like others. So Jacob (peace be upon him) sent his sons to buy grain, and they were ten men, after he learned that the king of Egypt was selling food. God the Exalted says, informing of their condition: ﴿And the brothers of Joseph came﴾, that is, from the land of Canaan, ﴿and they entered upon him﴾, that is, upon Joseph, ﴿and he recognized them, but they did not recognize him﴾, that is, they did not know him because of his change through advancing age and the change of his circumstances. And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And when he had furnished them with their provisions﴾, that is, he measured out for them and loaded each one's camel after he had honoured them to the utmost honour. ﴿He said: Bring me a brother of yours from your father﴾. There is no doubt that he had asked them about their circumstances, so they informed him about their father and his children in detail, and therefore he said to them, ﴿Bring me a brother of yours from your father﴾, and he is Benjamin. He encouraged them to do so by saying: ﴿Do you not see that I give full measure and that I am the best of hosts?﴾, that is, the best of hosts to whomever lodges with them. ﴿But if you bring him not to me, there will be no measure for you with me, nor shall you come near me.﴾ After this insistence upon them, they answered him with what God the Exalted informed of concerning them, by His saying: ﴿They said: We will seek to persuade his father concerning him, and we will certainly do it.﴾, that is, we will exert our utmost effort in seeking him until we bring him. ﴿And we will certainly do it﴾, as we have told you.

And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And he said to his servants: Put their merchandise back into their saddlebags﴾ informs of the words of Joseph to his attendants: put their silver coins with which they bought the food into their saddlebags without their noticing, ﴿so that they may recognize it when they return to their family, so that perhaps they will come back.﴾ All this was out of Joseph's desire to bring his full brother, so he made the return of the silver coins a means to that, because when they found them they would be embarrassed to take them, and so they would return with them. And they came with their brother, and this was the request of Joseph (peace be upon him), which God fulfilled.

**Guidance from the verses:**

1- The wondrous arrangement of God the Exalted: the king's dream, Joseph's interpretation of it, and its coming to pass as he interpreted it, was an arrangement for Joseph's authority, then for the coming of his brothers seeking food for their families, and so that the following chain of events would be completed. There is no god but God, and no lord besides Him.

2- The excellent planning of Joseph (peace be upon him) in bringing his brother Benjamin, as a preparation for bringing the whole family.

3- The effect of faith on conduct: Joseph knew that his brothers would not permit themselves to consume property not rightfully theirs, so he put the silver coins into their saddlebags so that they would return with them, together with their brother whom he wished to bring.

Meaning of the Verses:

The noble context continues speaking of Yusuf and his brothers. The Exalted says, informing of the return of Yusuf's brothers from Egypt to the land of Canaan in Palestine: ﴿So when they returned to their father﴾, that is, Ya'qub (peace be upon him), ﴿they said: "O our father, the measure has been withheld from us, so send our brother with us that we may obtain a measure, and indeed we will be its guardians"﴾, that is, the king of Egypt has withheld the measure from us unless we bring our brother Binyamin, ﴿so send with us our brother that we may obtain [provision], and indeed we will guard him﴾ from any harm under any circumstances. Ya'qub (peace be upon him) answered them with what the Exalted related about him, saying: ﴿He said: "Shall I entrust him to you except as I entrusted you with his brother before?"﴾, that is, I do not entrust him to you ﴿except as I entrusted you with his brother before﴾, meaning Yusuf, when they took him to the desert. ﴿But God is the best guardian, and He is the most merciful of the merciful﴾. This discussion took place between them upon their arrival and before opening their goods. As for after opening them, they said what the Exalted has informed of in His words: ﴿And when they opened their goods, they found their merchandise had been returned to them﴾, that is, their money, ﴿they said: "O our father, what more could we desire? This is our merchandise returned to us. So we will bring provisions for our family, and guard our brother, and receive an extra camel's load. Ya'qub answered them with what the Exalted related of him: ﴿He said: "I will never send him with you until you give me a firm covenant in God's name that you will surely bring him back to me, unless you are surrounded [by enemies]"﴾, that is, until you give me a covenant confirmed by oath that you will bring him to me, ﴿unless you are encompassed﴾ by an enemy or the like so that you all perish. So they gave him the covenant and pledge he asked of them. The Exalted said: ﴿And when they had given their covenant, he said: "God is witness over what we say"﴾, that is, a witness over me and over you. So he called God the Exalted to witness their covenant.

When they intended to travel to Egypt, paternal tenderness and faithful mercy moved him to say to them what the Exalted has related of him: ﴿And he said: "O my sons, do not enter by one gate, but enter by different gates"﴾, that is, do not enter, you being eleven men, through one gate, lest the evil eye swiftly reach you; rather, enter through several gates so that you do not appear as one group, the sons of one man, and so the eye of the envious does not strike you. Then he said: ﴿Yet I cannot avail you anything against God; judgment belongs only to God﴾, and so it is ﴿Whatever He wills happens﴾. ﴿In Him I have put my trust﴾, that is, I have entrusted my affair to Him, ﴿and in Him let the trusting put their trust﴾, that is, let those who trust entrust themselves to Him.

Guidance from the Verses:

1- Demonstration of the extent of Ya'qub's (peace be upon him) reliance upon God, his trust in his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, and his knowledge of His names and attributes; and how could it be otherwise, since he is one of God's prophets and messengers, peace be upon them.

2- The permissibility of taking a firm covenant in important matters, even from the closest of people such as one's sons, for example.

3- There is no harm in a believer's apprehension of being struck by the evil eye and taking precautions to guard against it, while believing that this avails nothing against God, and that judgment belongs to God alone, with no partner in His creation in this.

4- The obligation to rely upon God the Exalted, to carry out the action that has been determined, and to entrust the outcome of whatever happens to God the Exalted.

"Ma nabghi" (ما نبغي): that is, what do we seek [of anything more]?

"Wa nazdadu kayla bayir" (ونزداد كيل بعير): that is, instead of being ten, we will receive eleven, a camel's load for each one of us.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 12, verses 68–72:

Explanation of the words:

*Illa hajatan fi nafs Ya'qub* (except a need in the soul of Ya'qub): it was the desire to ward off the evil eye from his sons, out of compassion for them.

*Awa ilayhi akhahu* (he took his brother to himself): that is, he embraced him during the meal and during the night's lodging.

*Fa la tabta'is* (so do not grieve): that is, do not be sad.

*Ja'ala al-siqaya* (he put the drinking-cup): that is, the king's sa' (measure), which was of gold; he used to drink from it, and then he made it a measure with which he measured out grain.

*Adhdhana mu'adhdhin* (a caller called out): a crier cried out.

*Ayyatuha al-'ir* (O caravan): that is, the company of travellers.

*Sawa' al-malik* (the king's measure): that is, the sa' of the king. The sa' and the sawa' have one meaning.

*Wa ana bihi za'im* (and I am its guarantor): that is, I am a surety for bringing the camel's load.

Meaning of the verses:

The discourse continues concerning the brothers of Yusuf. He had charged them that, when they reached the land of Egypt, they should not enter through one gate but through several gates, out of fear of the evil eye upon them. They arrived and acted upon their father's counsel. Allah the Exalted says, reporting about them: ﴿And when they entered from where their father had commanded them, it did not avail them anything against Allah; it was only a need in the soul of Ya'qub which he fulfilled.﴾ That is, their entering through separate gates ﴿against Allah﴾, that is, against His decree, ﴿in anything, except a need﴾, that is, but a need ﴿in the soul of Ya'qub﴾, which was the fear of the evil eye upon them, ﴿which he fulfilled﴾, that is, nothing more.

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And indeed, he was a possessor of knowledge because of what We had taught him﴾ is a praise of Ya'qub, meaning that he was truly a man of knowledge and action, owing to Our teaching him. And His saying: ﴿But most of the people do not know﴾ is, as He the Mighty and Majestic has informed, that most people do not know about Allah the Exalted the attributes of His majesty and perfection, what He loves and what He dislikes, the paths to attaining His good pleasure and obtaining His approval and love, and what of that is forbidden to the servant that he should guard against. This is what the first verse [68] indicates.

As for the second verse: Allah the Exalted has informed that when the brothers of Yusuf entered upon him in his dwelling, he took his brother to himself, that is, his full brother, who was Benjamin. When the time of sleep came, he placed each two of them in a room, and they were eleven men, and Benjamin remained, so he said, "This one sleeps with me." When he took him to himself on his bed, he informed him that he was his brother Yusuf, and told him not to grieve over what his brothers had done with their father and with their brother Yusuf. He also informed him that he would devise a way to keep him with himself, so he should not be concerned about that and should not tell his brothers anything of this. This is what the second verse indicates, which is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when they entered upon Yusuf, he took his brother to himself, saying, "Indeed, I am your brother, so do not be distressed by what they used to do."﴾

As for the third verse [70]: it includes the report of Yusuf's plan to keep his brother with himself without them. When he had equipped them with their provision, that is, he measured out food for them and supplied them with what they needed after honouring them, he placed, by a hidden means that they did not perceive, the king's drinking-cup, which is the sa' or sawa', and it is a vessel of gold from which he used to drink; then he made a measuring instrument specific to the king, known as the king's sawa' or sa'. He placed it in the baggage of his brother Benjamin.

Then, when the caravan set out and had gone a few paces, a caller called out, saying, "O caravan! Indeed, you are thieves." This is what the noble verse contains, for He, exalted is He, said: ﴿So when he had furnished them with their provisions, he placed the drinking-cup in the baggage of his brother; then a crier called out, "O caravan, indeed you are thieves!"﴾ Allah the Exalted says, reporting about them: ﴿They said, while turning toward them, "What is it that you are missing?"﴾ They answered with their saying: ﴿"We are missing the king's measure, and for whoever brings it is a camel's load"﴾, that is, as a reward for him, ﴿"and I am its guarantor"﴾, that is, I am surety for giving him the camel's load.

Guidance from the verses:

1. Clarification of the virtue of knowledge and of its people.
2. Affirmation of the reality that most people do not know.
3. The good planning of Yusuf to keep his brother with him after his brothers had gone.
4. The permissibility of giving rewards to one who performs a specific task, which in jurisprudence is *ju'ala* (a reward-contract).
5. The permissibility of *kafala* (suretyship), and the surety bears the liability.

And His saying: ﴿But most of the people do not know﴾ is, as He the Mighty and Majestic has informed, that most people do not know about Allah the Exalted the attributes of His majesty and perfection, what He loves and what He dislikes, the paths to attaining His good pleasure and obtaining His approval and love, and what of that is forbidden to the servant that he should guard against. This is what the first verse [68] indicates.

As for the second verse: Allah the Exalted has informed that when the brothers of Yusuf entered upon him in his dwelling, he took his brother to himself, that is, his full brother, who was Benjamin. When the time of sleep came, he placed each two of them in a room, and they were eleven men, and Benjamin remained, so he said, "This one sleeps with me." When he took him to himself on his bed, he informed him that he was his brother Yusuf, and told him not to grieve over what his brothers had done with their father and with their brother Yusuf. He also informed him that he would devise a way to keep him with himself, so he should not be concerned about that and should not tell his brothers anything of this. This is what the second verse indicates, which is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when they entered upon Yusuf, he took his brother to himself, saying, "Indeed, I am your brother, so do not be distressed by what they used to do."﴾

As for the third verse [70]: it includes the report of Yusuf's plan to keep his brother with himself without them. When he had equipped them with their provision, that is, he measured out food for them and supplied them with what they needed after honouring them, he placed, by a hidden means that they did not perceive, the king's drinking-cup, which is the sa' or sawa', and it is a vessel of gold from which he used to drink; then he made a measuring instrument specific to the king, known as the king's sawa' or sa'. He placed it in the baggage of his brother Benjamin.

Then, when the caravan set out and had gone a few paces, a caller called out, saying, "O caravan! Indeed, you are thieves." This is what the noble verse contains, for He, exalted is He, said: ﴿So when he had furnished them with their provisions, he placed the drinking-cup in the baggage of his brother; then a crier called out, "O caravan, indeed you are thieves!"﴾ Allah the Exalted says, reporting about them: ﴿They said, while turning toward them, "What is it that you are missing?"﴾ They answered with their saying: ﴿"We are missing the king's measure, and for whoever brings it is a camel's load"﴾, that is, as a reward for him, ﴿"and I am its guarantor"﴾, that is, I am surety for giving him the camel's load.

Guidance from the verses:

1. Clarification of the virtue of knowledge and of its people.
2. Affirmation of the reality that most people do not know.
3. The good planning of Yusuf to keep his brother with him after his brothers had gone.
4. The permissibility of giving rewards to one who performs a specific task, which in jurisprudence is *ju'ala* (a reward-contract).
5. The permissibility of *kafala* (suretyship), and the surety bears the liability.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 12, verses 73–76:

Explanation of the words:

"Tallahi" (by God): i.e., by God.

"Li-nufsida fil-ard" (to cause corruption in the land): i.e., by committing sins and falling into wrongdoing.

"Wa ma kunna sariqin" (and we were never thieves): i.e., we did not steal the goblet, just as we have never stolen the property of anyone before.

"Man wujida fi rahlihi fahuwa jaza'uhu" (whoever is found with it in his baggage, he is its recompense): i.e., he is taken as a slave for the theft.

"Kadhalika najzi al-zalimin" (thus do we recompense the wrongdoers): i.e., in our law.

"Fi wi'a' akhihi" (in the bag of his brother): i.e., in the bag of his brother, which was in his baggage.

"Kadhalika kidna li-Yusuf" (thus did We plan for Joseph): i.e., We facilitated for him this scheme by which he reached a praiseworthy end.

"Fi din al-malik" (in the law of the king): i.e., in his legislation, since he would beat the thief and make him pay a penalty equal to what he stole.

"Narfa'u darajatin man nasha'" (We raise in degrees whom We will): i.e., as We raised Joseph, peace be upon him.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues to speak of Joseph and his brothers. When the theft of the king's goblet was announced, the caravan was halted for inspection, and a reward was declared for whoever brings the goblet, guaranteed to be paid, the brothers of Joseph said what God, exalted is He, related about them: "They said, 'By God, you know that we did not come to cause corruption in the land'": i.e., by theft and falling into sins; we came only for provisions. "'And we were never thieves'": i.e., at any time. Here the king's men, answering their denial with what God, exalted is He, related, said: "They said, 'Then what is its penalty, if you are liars?'" The brothers answered with what God, exalted is He, related about them in His saying: "They said, 'Its penalty is: whoever is found with it in his baggage, he himself is its penalty.'" They meant that a thief is enslaved, i.e., becomes owned through the theft. His saying "Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers" means: in our law. Here Joseph himself began to search the bags of his brothers in search of the goblet, starting with their bags one by one, and he searched the bag of his brother Benjamin last, to dispel accusation and collusion in the affair, until he extracted it from the bag of his brother which was in his baggage. This is what His saying, exalted is He, indicates: "So he began with their bags before the bag of his brother, then he brought it out from the bag of his brother." And His saying, exalted is He: "Thus did We plan for Joseph": i.e., thus did We facilitate for him this scheme by which he reached a praiseworthy end, not blameworthy. And His saying, exalted is He: "He could not have taken his brother under the law of the king": i.e., it was not in the law of Egypt that he take his brother as a slave for theft; rather the thief is beaten and made to pay only. "Unless God wills": a matter, so it comes to be. And His saying, exalted is He: "We raise in degrees whom We will": i.e., in knowledge, as We raised Joseph. "And over every possessor of knowledge is one who knows": among people, "[is] the All-Knowing," until knowledge ends with God, exalted is He, who is the All-Knowing, than whom none knows more; rather all knowledge is His and from Him, and were it not for Him no one would know anything.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- The permissibility of swearing by God, exalted is He, when there is need.

2- The legitimacy of warding off accusation from an innocent self.

3- Knowing the ruling on theft in the law of Ya'qub, peace be upon him.

4- Clarification of the excellence of God's management for His friends.

5- Clarification of the ruling on theft in Egyptian law in the time of Joseph, peace be upon him.

6- The loftiness of Joseph's station in knowledge, peace be upon him.

7- Establishing the principle "And over every possessor of knowledge is one who knows": until knowledge ends with God, exalted is He.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 12, verses 77–79:

Explanation of the words:

"In yasriq": that is, he takes the drinking-cup secretly from its place of safekeeping.

"Faqad saraqa akhun lahu": that is, Yusuf in his childhood.

"Fa-asarraha Yusuf fi nafsihi": that is, he concealed this accusation within himself.

"Wa lam yubdiha lahum": that is, he did not reveal it to them.

"Antum sharr makanan": that is, in rank you are worse than the one you accused of theft.

"Bima tasifun": that is, in the reality of what you describe, that is, what you mention.

"Aban shaykhan kabiran": that is, Ya'qub, peace be upon him.

"Ma'adh Allah": that is, we seek refuge in God from taking anyone in whose possession we did not find our property.

"Mata'ana": that is, the drinking-cup.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues in the discussion between Yusuf, peace be upon him, and his brothers. After Yusuf had brought the cup out of his brother's belongings, and it was apparently established that Binyamin had stolen, his brothers said what God related of them in His words: ﴿They said, "If he has stolen, a brother of his has stolen before."﴾ That is, if Binyamin has stolen as you have determined, then there is no wonder, for a brother of his stole before, meaning Yusuf in his childhood. He used to steal food and give it to the needy, and he stole an idol of his mother's father and broke it so that it would not be worshipped; this is not forbidden or blameworthy theft, rather it is praiseworthy. As for His words, may He be exalted, ﴿So Yusuf concealed it within himself and did not reveal it to them﴾: that is, Yusuf kept their statement, ﴿a brother of his has stolen before,﴾ secret and did not reveal it to them, and in rejecting their mistaken statement he said: ﴿You are worse in position﴾: that is, worse in rank than those you accused of theft. ﴿And God is most knowing of what you describe﴾: that is, of the reality of what you mention. When they heard Yusuf's words, and there was in them a kind of severity and harshness, they said, seeking to placate Yusuf and move his mercy, with what God related of them in His words: ﴿They said, "O Chieftain, indeed he has a father, an elderly man of great age,"﴾ that is, our brother has a father of advanced years, whom it grieves him to be separated from and whom he cannot bear to lose. ﴿So take one of us in his place. Indeed, we see you are of the good-doers.﴾ that is, take one of us instead of him; and one like you does such a thing, for it is kindness, and you are among the good-doers. He answered them with what God related in His words: ﴿He said, "We seek refuge in God from taking anyone except him in whose possession we found our property; indeed, we would then be wrongdoers."﴾ that is, we seek refuge in God, since if we took one who did not commit the offence and left the one who did, that is, who stole, we would then be wrongdoers, and this is what we do not accept and do not agree to.

Lessons from the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- The legitimacy of apologising for a mistake.

2- The forbearing person may be compelled to say what he would not have said had it not been for the evil he was confronted with.

3- The legitimacy of seeking mercy and compassion for one who needs it, in hope that he will be shown mercy and compassion.

4- The prohibition of leaving the offender and taking another in his place, for this is a forbidden wrong.

From the guidance of the verses:

2- The forbearing person may be compelled to say what he would not have said had it not been for the evil he was confronted with.

Meaning of the verses:

After Joseph seized their brother on the charge of theft and did not accept their entreaties to take another in his place, they withdrew to one side to consider their affair. 6. Expressing grief, sorrow, and complaint to God, exalted is He.
