Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 12, verses 89–93:

Explanation of the words:

"إذ أنتم جاهلون" (Idh antum jahiluna): i.e., you do not know what the outcome of Yusuf's affair will be.

"قد منّ الله علينا" (Qad manna Allahu 'alayna): i.e., Allah has bestowed favor upon us by bringing us together after a long separation of which you were the cause.

"من يتق ويصبر" (Man yattaqi wa yasbir): i.e., whoever fears Allah, so that he does not disobey Him, and endures what befalls him of hardship and toil.

"لقد آثرك الله علينا" (Laqad athraka Allahu 'alayna): i.e., Allah has preferred you over us by the bounties and perfection with which He has favored you.

"لا تثريب عليكم" (La tathriba 'alaykum): i.e., there is no blame or reproach upon you.

Meaning of the verses:

The discourse continues concerning Yusuf and his brothers. When they came to him from the land of Canaan, by the command of their father, and complained to him of the hardship they were in, saying, "Harm has touched us, and we have come with meager merchandise," his heart was softened upon hearing this from them, his eyes overflowed with tears, and he wished to end the concealment he had maintained, which was hiding his state from them. So he said to them: ﴿He said, "Do you know what you did with Yusuf and his brother, when you were ignorant?"﴾ He reminded them of what they had done to him: throwing him into the well and selling him as a slave, and by that separating him from his father and his full brother. His saying ﴿when you were ignorant﴾ means that you did not know what Yusuf's affair would come to. Here they said in astonishment and amazement: ﴿"Are you indeed Yusuf?"﴾ He answered them, saying what Allah the Exalted related of him: ﴿"I am Yusuf, and this is my brother. Allah has certainly favored us."﴾ That is, He bestowed His favor upon us and brought us together in the best condition. Then he said: ﴿"Indeed, whoever fears Allah and is patient—"﴾ that is, whoever fears Allah, reverencing Him, establishes His obligations, avoids His prohibitions, and is patient in that and in what He tests him with. ﴿"Then indeed, Allah does not waste the reward of the good-doers."﴾ That is, those who are obedient to their Lord and submit to Him outwardly and inwardly. Here they said to him what Allah the Exalted related of them: ﴿"By Allah, Allah has certainly preferred you over us"﴾ that is, in knowledge, action and virtue, ﴿"and we were indeed sinners."﴾ regarding what we did to you. This was their repentance, so he said to them: ﴿"No reproach will be upon you today."﴾ That is, no censure, no blame, and no mention of what you did, because that would cause harm. ﴿"May Allah forgive you, and He is the most merciful of the merciful."﴾ He asked Allah to forgive him and them, and praised Allah as the most merciful of the merciful, seeking His mercy for himself and his brothers. Then he asked them about his father, and they informed him that he had gone blind from grief over him. So he said: ﴿"Take this shirt of mine and cast it over my father's face; he will regain his sight."﴾ That is, he will return to seeing as he was. ﴿"And bring me your whole family."﴾ He meant his parents, the women, the children and the grandchildren. This was a complete transfer of the noble family from the land of Canaan to the land of Egypt, by the arrangement of Allah, the Mighty, the Wise.

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Establishing the principle that acts of disobedience result only from ignorance of Allah, His majesty, His laws, His promise and His threat.

2- The virtue of piety and patience and the good outcome they bring.

3- The virtue of pardon and forgiveness, and leaving off reproaching a relative who has wronged you.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 12, verses 89–93:

Explanation of the words:

"إذ أنتم جاهلون" (Idh antum jahiluna): i.e., you do not know what the outcome of Yusuf's affair will be.

"قد منّ الله علينا" (Qad manna Allahu 'alayna): i.e., Allah has bestowed favor upon us by bringing us together after a long separation of which you were the cause.

"من يتق ويصبر" (Man yattaqi wa yasbir): i.e., whoever fears Allah, so that he does not disobey Him, and endures what befalls him of hardship and toil.

"لقد آثرك الله علينا" (Laqad athraka Allahu 'alayna): i.e., Allah has preferred you over us by the bounties and perfection with which He has favored you.

"لا تثريب عليكم" (La tathriba 'alaykum): i.e., there is no blame or reproach upon you.

Meaning of the verses:

The discourse continues concerning Yusuf and his brothers. When they came to him from the land of Canaan, by the command of their father, and complained to him of the hardship they were in, saying, "Harm has touched us, and we have come with meager merchandise," his heart was softened upon hearing this from them, his eyes overflowed with tears, and he wished to end the concealment he had maintained, which was hiding his state from them. So he said to them: ﴿He said, "Do you know what you did with Yusuf and his brother, when you were ignorant?"﴾ He reminded them of what they had done to him: throwing him into the well and selling him as a slave, and by that separating him from his father and his full brother. His saying ﴿when you were ignorant﴾ means that you did not know what Yusuf's affair would come to. Here they said in astonishment and amazement: ﴿"Are you indeed Yusuf?"﴾ He answered them, saying what Allah the Exalted related of him: ﴿"I am Yusuf, and this is my brother. Allah has certainly favored us."﴾ That is, He bestowed His favor upon us and brought us together in the best condition. Then he said: ﴿"Indeed, whoever fears Allah and is patient—"﴾ that is, whoever fears Allah, reverencing Him, establishes His obligations, avoids His prohibitions, and is patient in that and in what He tests him with. ﴿"Then indeed, Allah does not waste the reward of the good-doers."﴾ That is, those who are obedient to their Lord and submit to Him outwardly and inwardly. Here they said to him what Allah the Exalted related of them: ﴿"By Allah, Allah has certainly preferred you over us"﴾ that is, in knowledge, action and virtue, ﴿"and we were indeed sinners."﴾ regarding what we did to you. This was their repentance, so he said to them: ﴿"No reproach will be upon you today."﴾ That is, no censure, no blame, and no mention of what you did, because that would cause harm. ﴿"May Allah forgive you, and He is the most merciful of the merciful."﴾ He asked Allah to forgive him and them, and praised Allah as the most merciful of the merciful, seeking His mercy for himself and his brothers. Then he asked them about his father, and they informed him that he had gone blind from grief over him. So he said: ﴿"Take this shirt of mine and cast it over my father's face; he will regain his sight."﴾ That is, he will return to seeing as he was. ﴿"And bring me your whole family."﴾ He meant his parents, the women, the children and the grandchildren. This was a complete transfer of the noble family from the land of Canaan to the land of Egypt, by the arrangement of Allah, the Mighty, the Wise.

2- The virtue of piety and patience and the good outcome they bring.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 12, verse 94–100:

Explanation of the words:

﴿ولما فصلت العير﴾: i.e., the caravan departed from the outskirts of Egypt, heading towards the land of Palestine.

﴿إني لأجد ريح يوسف﴾: I smell it, because the wind carried it to him by the command of God, the Exalted.

﴿لولا أن تفندّون﴾: i.e., you consider me feeble-minded (tufannidun, you deem me senile or foolish); you would have believed me, for I have found the scent of Yusuf.

﴿إنك لفي ضلالك القديم﴾: i.e., your error, through your excessive love for Yusuf.

﴿فلما أن جاء البشير﴾: he is Yahuda (Judah), who carried to him the shirt smeared with false blood.

﴿فارتد بصيراً﴾: i.e., he returned to sight.

﴿سوف استغفر لكم ربي﴾: he deferred seeking forgiveness for them until the last part of the night, or until the night of Friday.

﴿على العرش﴾: i.e., the throne (al-sarir, the couch).

﴿وخروا له سجداً﴾: i.e., they prostrated to him in greeting and honour.

﴿من البدو﴾: i.e., the desert, the desert of Syria (Badiyat al-Sham).

﴿من بعد أن نزغ﴾: i.e., corrupted.

﴿لطيف لما يشاء﴾: i.e., gentle in His management towards whomever He wills of His servants, as He was gentle with Yusuf.

Meaning of the verses:

These are the final parts of the story of Yusuf, peace be upon him. After he sent his shirt to his father, his brother Yahuda carried it within the caravan heading to the land of Canaan. When the caravan departed from the outskirts of Egypt, the east wind carried the scent of Yusuf to his father, and he said: ﴿Indeed, I smell the scent of Yusuf; if you did not think me senile, you would believe me,﴾ i.e., you would deem me feeble-minded, had you believed me, for I smell it. Those present in his assembly from the family members, and those who did not know the news of Yusuf in Egypt, said to him: ﴿By God, you are surely in your old error,﴾ i.e., your error through your excessive love for Yusuf.

The caravan continued its journey, and after some days it arrived. Yahuda came carrying the shirt and cast it upon the face of Yaqub, and he regained his sight, as Yusuf had told his brothers in Egypt. Here he addressed his sons with the words that God, the Exalted, related in His saying: ﴿Did I not tell you that I know from God what you do not know?﴾ i.e., I know of God's gentleness, good management, mercy and bounty what you do not know. Here they asked their father to pardon them and to ask their Lord for forgiveness, as God, the Exalted, related: ﴿They said, "O our father, ask forgiveness for our sins; indeed we have been mistaken."﴾ ﴿He said, "I will ask my Lord for forgiveness for you; indeed He is the Forgiving, the Merciful."﴾ He deferred their request for forgiveness until the time of acceptance, such as the last part of the night, the time of dawn, or the day of Friday. In execution of Yusuf's command to his brothers to bring their entire family to him, the family, with all its members, travelled as migrants to Egypt. Yusuf, the king of Egypt, and thousands of state officials and notables of the land were there to receive them. Yusuf had a tent or pavilion erected for them, and the migrating family reached the outskirts of the Egyptian territories while Yusuf was in his pavilion. ﴿So when they entered upon Yusuf, he drew his parents to himself,﴾ i.e., he took them into his procession. ﴿And he said, "Enter Egypt, if God wills, in security."﴾ When they reached the palace and entered, ﴿he raised his parents﴾, his mother and father, ﴿upon the throne﴾, the royal couch, ﴿and they fell down before him in prostration,﴾ as greeting and honour. Here Yusuf said: ﴿O my father, this is the interpretation of my vision from before; my Lord has made it come true,﴾ for in his youth he had seen eleven stars and the sun and the moon prostrating to him.

As for His saying: ﴿And He was certainly good to me when He took me out of prison and brought you from the desert after Satan had caused strife between me and my brothers,﴾ this is praise of God for His blessings and a reminder to those present of the event and of God's kindnesses within it. Out of the nobility of Yusuf's soul and the loftiness of his manners, he did not say, "He was good to me when He took me out of the well," so as not to remind them of what would pain them, but said "out of the prison." By his words "brought you from the desert" he means from the land of Canaan. He attributed the mischief that came from his brothers to Satan, as a softening of the atmosphere and an effort to remove sorrow from the hearts of his brothers. He ended the account of blessing with the greatest joy: ﴿Indeed my Lord is Gentle with what He wills; indeed He is the Knowing,﴾ i.e., of His creation, ﴿the Wise﴾ in His management and His craftsmanship.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- A great sign: the wind carrying the scent of Yusuf over great distances.

2- Another sign: the return of Yaqub's sight after blindness, as soon as the shirt was cast upon his face.

3- The generosity of Yaqub and the goodness of his pardon and forgiveness towards his sons, when he asked their Lord to forgive them, and He forgave them.

4- The permissibility of going outside the city to receive people of perfection and virtue, such as pilgrims, for example.

5- The truthfulness of the vision of Yusuf, peace be upon him, for it came true literally: he sat on his throne and his parents and brothers fell down before him in prostration.

6- The interpretation of a dream may be delayed by decades, for the vision of Yusuf was delayed forty years.

7- The manifestations of divine kindness and lordly mercies in this story appear in wondrous forms.

﴿لولا أن تفندّون﴾: i.e., you consider me feeble-minded (tufannidun, you deem me senile or foolish); you would have believed me, for I have found the scent of Yusuf.

﴿إنك لفي ضلالك القديم﴾: i.e., your error, through your excessive love for Yusuf.

﴿فلما أن جاء البشير﴾: he is Yahuda (Judah), who carried to him the shirt smeared with false blood.

﴿فارتد بصيراً﴾: i.e., he returned to sight.

﴿سوف استغفر لكم ربي﴾: he deferred seeking forgiveness for them until the last part of the night, or until the night of Friday.

﴿على العرش﴾: i.e., the throne (al-sarir, the couch).

﴿وخروا له سجداً﴾: i.e., they prostrated to him in greeting and honour.

﴿من البدو﴾: i.e., the desert, the desert of Syria (Badiyat al-Sham).

﴿من بعد أن نزغ﴾: i.e., corrupted.

﴿لطيف لما يشاء﴾: i.e., gentle in His management towards whomever He wills of His servants, as He was gentle with Yusuf.

Meaning of the verses:

These are the final parts of the story of Yusuf, peace be upon him. After he sent his shirt to his father, his brother Yahuda carried it within the caravan heading to the land of Canaan. When the caravan departed from the outskirts of Egypt, the east wind carried the scent of Yusuf to his father, and he said: ﴿Indeed, I smell the scent of Yusuf; if you did not think me senile, you would believe me,﴾ i.e., you would deem me feeble-minded, had you believed me, for I smell it. Those present in his assembly from the family members, and those who did not know the news of Yusuf in Egypt, said to him: ﴿By God, you are surely in your old error,﴾ i.e., your error through your excessive love for Yusuf.

The caravan continued its journey, and after some days it arrived. Yahuda came carrying the shirt and cast it upon the face of Yaqub, and he regained his sight, as Yusuf had told his brothers in Egypt. Here he addressed his sons with the words that God, the Exalted, related in His saying: ﴿Did I not tell you that I know from God what you do not know?﴾ i.e., I know of God's gentleness, good management, mercy and bounty what you do not know. Here they asked their father to pardon them and to ask their Lord for forgiveness, as God, the Exalted, related: ﴿They said, "O our father, ask forgiveness for our sins; indeed we have been mistaken."﴾ ﴿He said, "I will ask my Lord for forgiveness for you; indeed He is the Forgiving, the Merciful."﴾ He deferred their request for forgiveness until the time of acceptance, such as the last part of the night, the time of dawn, or the day of Friday. In execution of Yusuf's command to his brothers to bring their entire family to him, the family, with all its members, travelled as migrants to Egypt. Yusuf, the king of Egypt, and thousands of state officials and notables of the land were there to receive them. Yusuf had a tent or pavilion erected for them, and the migrating family reached the outskirts of the Egyptian territories while Yusuf was in his pavilion. ﴿So when they entered upon Yusuf, he drew his parents to himself,﴾ i.e., he took them into his procession. ﴿And he said, "Enter Egypt, if God wills, in security."﴾ When they reached the palace and entered, ﴿he raised his parents﴾, his mother and father, ﴿upon the throne﴾, the royal couch, ﴿and they fell down before him in prostration,﴾ as greeting and honour. Here Yusuf said: ﴿O my father, this is the interpretation of my vision from before; my Lord has made it come true,﴾ for in his youth he had seen eleven stars and the sun and the moon prostrating to him.

As for His saying: ﴿And He was certainly good to me when He took me out of prison and brought you from the desert after Satan had caused strife between me and my brothers,﴾ this is praise of God for His blessings and a reminder to those present of the event and of God's kindnesses within it. Out of the nobility of Yusuf's soul and the loftiness of his manners, he did not say, "He was good to me when He took me out of the well," so as not to remind them of what would pain them, but said "out of the prison." By his words "brought you from the desert" he means from the land of Canaan. He attributed the mischief that came from his brothers to Satan, as a softening of the atmosphere and an effort to remove sorrow from the hearts of his brothers. He ended the account of blessing with the greatest joy: ﴿Indeed my Lord is Gentle with what He wills; indeed He is the Knowing,﴾ i.e., of His creation, ﴿the Wise﴾ in His management and His craftsmanship.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- A great sign: the wind carrying the scent of Yusuf over great distances.

2- Another sign: the return of Yaqub's sight after blindness, as soon as the shirt was cast upon his face.

3- The generosity of Yaqub and the goodness of his pardon and forgiveness towards his sons, when he asked their Lord to forgive them, and He forgave them.

4- The permissibility of going outside the city to receive people of perfection and virtue, such as pilgrims, for example.

5- The truthfulness of the vision of Yusuf, peace be upon him, for it came true literally: he sat on his throne and his parents and brothers fell down before him in prostration.

6- The interpretation of a dream may be delayed by decades, for the vision of Yusuf was delayed forty years.

7- The manifestations of divine kindness and lordly mercies in this story appear in wondrous forms.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 12, verse 101:

Explanation of the words:

Rabb (Lord): that is, "O my Lord, my Creator, my Provider, the Master of my affairs, and my Worshipped One, other than whom I have no deity."

Min al-mulk (of the kingdom): that is, of part of the kingdom, since he had become king of Egypt only.

Ta'wil al-ahadith (the interpretation of narratives): the interpretation of dreams.

Fatir al-samawat wa'l-ard (Originator of the heavens and the earth): that is, their Creator, without any previous pattern.

Anta waliyyi (You are my Guardian): that is, the one who manages my affairs in both lives, the worldly life and the Hereafter.

The meaning of the noble verse:

This is the end of the account of the story of Yusuf. After Allah the Exalted had reunited him with all the members of his family, and opened for him from the treasuries of His mercy what He opened, and the hardships were turned into radiance: the hardship of being thrown into the well, of being sold as a slave for a paltry price, of the trial of the chieftain's wife, and of imprisonment for seven years, were transformed into radiance: kingship and dominion, honour and elevation, wealth and affluence, gathering and harmony, and above all that, knowledge bestowed directly from Allah (al-'ilm al-ladunni), divine revelation, and the interpretation of narratives. After Allah the Exalted took his father, accepted the repentance of his brothers, prepared them for prophethood and made them prophets, the soul of Yusuf yearned for the Supreme Kingdom, for the righteous companionship, for the company of the good, his pure forefathers Ibrahim, Ishaq and Ya'qub. He raised his hands to his Lord and said: ﴿My Lord, You have given me [some] of the kingdom and taught me [something] of the interpretation of narratives. Originator of the heavens and the earth, You are my Guardian in this world and the Hereafter. Cause me to die a Muslim and join me with the righteous.﴾ Allah the Exalted answered his supplication, and he did not remain long before death came to him; he departed and joined his forefathers and his righteous brethren. So peace be upon him, upon them, and upon every righteous person in the earth and the heavens, and peace upon the messengers, and praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds.

Guidance from the verse:

Among the guidance of the verse:

1- The legitimacy of calling upon Allah the Exalted and seeking nearness to Him through His names and attributes.

2- The legitimacy of turning away from the world and having no desire for it when it is attained and one is empowered over it.

3- The virtue of longing for Allah and yearning for the companionship of the righteous in the Supreme Kingdom.

4- The legitimacy of asking for death if it is not due to harm or weariness of worship, or a desire for rest, based on the hadith "None of you should wish for death because of a harm that has befallen him," which is authentic. Rather, it is out of longing for Allah the Exalted and joining the righteous, turning away from this abode and yearning for the other, the Abode of Peace.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 12, verses 102–106:**

**Explanation of the words:**

*Dhalika* (that): a reference to what Allah related to His Messenger of the story of Yusuf and his brothers.

*Min anba' al-ghayb* (from the news of the unseen): that is, news of the unseen.

*Wa ma kunta ladayhim* (and you were not with them): that is, with the brothers of Yusuf.

*Idh ajma'u amrahum* (when they resolved their affair): that is, they agreed on casting Yusuf into the darkness of the well (*ghayabat al-jubb*).

*Wa hum yamkurun* (while they were scheming): that is, they were plotting to take him out and throw him into the well.

*Alayhi min ajr* (any reward for it): that is, for the Qur'an and conveying it, any wealth as a reward.

*In huwa illa dhikr* (it is nothing but a reminder): that is, it is nothing but a reminder, an admonition by which the believers are admonished.

**Meaning of the verses:**

After Allah related to His Messenger, through revelation (*wahy*), the story of Yusuf and his brothers, which is pure unseen knowledge, since neither the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) nor his people, the Arabs, knew anything of these historical events, especially as some of these events occurred in the darkness of the night, some in the darkness of the well, some behind curtains, some in the prison cells, some in the palaces of kings, some in the settled towns and some in the desert, and after the long passage of time and the lapse of ages. Having related what He related, He said to His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿That is among the news of the unseen﴾, that is, from the reports of the unseen, ﴿We reveal it to you﴾, that is, We inform you of it by way of revelation, ﴿and you were not with them when they resolved on their affair and were scheming﴾. He confirms His revelation to him by this, saying: you were not with the brothers of Yusuf at the time when they resolved upon ridding themselves of Yusuf at any cost, and they were scheming to remove him from before his father so that they might cast him into the darkness of the well, to be rid of him, since they saw that he had taken their father's face from them and had taken his tenderness and compassion to himself, excluding them.

And the statement of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Yet most people, though you should be eager, will not be believers﴾. He, the Exalted, informs him that belief in you, in what you have brought of revelation, in monotheism and in the Last Resurrection, and such narratives as this, are sufficient as evidence for the validity of your prophethood and for the obligation to believe in what you have brought and what you call to. Despite this, most people, even if you were eager for their faith, would not be believers. There are factors for this, the most prominent of which is that faith conflicts with the falsehood, evil and corruption to which they have become accustomed, especially their worldly desires and aims. And before that, whoever Allah has decreed wretchedness for will never believe under any circumstances. Therefore do not grieve and do not be distressed.

And the statement of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And you do not ask them any reward for it﴾, that is, for this Qur'an and for conveying it to them, any wealth. For if you were asking them a reward for reciting it to them and conveying it to them, that would be an obstacle to their accepting what you call them to. But since this is offered to them free of charge, there is no sense in their not believing except for what Allah has decreed of their loss; they are working toward reaching it.

And the statement of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿It is nothing but a reminder to the worlds﴾, that is, this Qur'an, with the guidance and light it carries, and your recitation of it, is nothing but a reminder, an admonition by which whoever hears it is admonished, from among the people of insight and faith, from among the worlds, those whom Allah, the Exalted, has prepared for happiness and perfection. And the statement of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And how many a sign there is in the heavens and the earth﴾, that is, many signs that point to Allah and to the obligation of worshipping Him and affirming His oneness are in them: in the heavens, such as the sun, the moon, the stars, the clouds and the rains; and in the earth, such as the mountains, the rivers, the trees and the various creatures. They pass by them morning and evening while being averse, not turning towards them nor reflecting upon them. Therefore they do not believe nor are they guided.

And the statement of Allah, the Exalted, in the last verse [106]: ﴿And most of them do not believe in Allah except that they associate others with Him﴾. He, the Exalted, informs His Messenger that most of those whom he calls to believe in Him and in what he has brought do not believe in Allah as Lord, Creator and Provider, except that they associate with Him idols and images that they worship. This is an established fact: if a Jew or a Christian were asked about the Creator, the Provider, the Giver of life, the Giver of death, and the Manager of the universe, he would say "Allah." But he associates with Him another whom he worships alongside Him. Such is the condition of the polytheists whom Allah, the Exalted, has told us about. And many of the ignorant people of this Qur'anic community call upon other than Allah, slaughter for other than Allah, and make vows to other than Allah, while they believe in Allah and in what His Messenger brought of monotheism, the Resurrection, the Recompense and the Law.

**Guidance of the verses (Hidayat al-Ayat):**

1. Establishing Muhammadan prophethood with the most truthful proof and the greatest argument.

2. Explaining Allah's judgment concerning people: that most of them do not believe, so the caller should not grieve or be distressed.

3. The call to Allah should be presented to people free of charge, and the caller's reward is with Allah, the One to whom he calls.

4. Condemnation of heedlessness and of failing to reflect upon the signs in the cosmos.

5. Explaining a established truth: that those other than the people of monotheism, even if they believe in Allah as Lord, Creator and Provider who manages affairs, most of them associate others with Him in some of His attributes and acts of worship.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 12, verses 107–109:

Explanation of the words:

*Ghashiyah min 'adhab Allah* (an overwhelming [calamity] from the punishment of God): i.e., a vengeance from His vengeance that overtakes them, meaning it encompasses them.

*Baghtah* (suddenly): all of a sudden, while they remain upon their polytheism and disbelief.

*Hadhihi sabili* (this is my way): i.e., my call and my method, which I follow.

*'Ala basirah* (with insight): i.e., with certain knowledge on my part.

*Wa subhan Allah* (and glory be to God): i.e., exalting God and sanctifying Him above having any partner in His dominion or any deity besides Him.

*Min ahl al-qura* (from the people of the towns): from the people of cities and metropolises, not from the people of the desert.

*Lilladhina ittaqaw* (for those who have taken God as their protection): i.e., God, by performing His obligations and abandoning His prohibitions.

*Afala ta'qilun* (will you not reason?): i.e., will these polytheists not reason about this which is recited to them and explained to them, so that they believe and affirm God's oneness.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues with the call to faith in divine revelation, to monotheism, to the Resurrection and to recompense, which are the great pillars of religion. God says: ﴿And most of them do not believe in God except that they associate others with Him﴾ [Yusuf: 106], and those who pass by many of the signs of God while turning away from them. Are these people then safe from ﴿that there should come upon them an overwhelming [calamity] from the punishment of God﴾, i.e., a punishment that envelops them and covers them with torment that cannot be withstood, ﴿or that the Hour should come upon them suddenly﴾, i.e., the Resurrection, ﴿while they are unaware﴾ of the time of its coming, so that the affliction is greatly magnified and the calamity becomes severe for them. And how can they feel safe, when is there anyone who can grant them safety other than God, the Exalted? Then what is wrong with them that they do not believe and do not fear, so that they might be saved from what is expected for them? This is what the first verse [107] indicates. As for the second, God commanded His Messenger to persist in his call, the call to good, he and the believers with him, saying: ﴿Say: This is my way﴾, i.e., say, O Messenger, to the people: this is my method in calling to my Lord, that He be believed in and worshipped alone, without any other. ﴿I call to God with insight﴾, i.e., with certain knowledge of whom I call to, of what I call with, and of the results that follow from this call, ﴿I and whoever follows me﴾ among the believers; we all call to God with insight.

And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And glory be to God﴾, i.e., say, "Glory be to God," meaning exalting Him above having any partner or son, and say likewise, declaring your innocence of polytheism and the polytheists: ﴿And I am not of the polytheists﴾. This is what the second verse indicates. As for the third verse, God informs His Messenger that He did not send before him any of the messengers, who were many, except men, i.e., not women and not angels, ﴿to whom We revealed from among the people of the towns﴾, i.e., the cities and metropolises. This is a refutation of their denial that the Messenger could be a man from among mankind. And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Have they not travelled through the land﴾, i.e., these deniers from Quraysh and others, ﴿so that they might look﴾ for lessons, ﴿and see how was the end of those before them, such as 'Ad and Thamud?﴾ For We destroyed them and saved those among them who were people of faith and monotheism, together with their messengers. This salvation is a fruit of faith and piety. ﴿And the Hereafter's abode is better for those who have taken God as their protection﴾, for it is the abode of lasting bliss and freedom from pains, afflictions, defects, senility, death and annihilation.

And His saying at the end of the verse, ﴿Will you not reason?﴾ rebukes those polytheists who insist on denial and association for their failure to reason and to understand what is recited to them, what they hear of the Qur'anic verses, and what they witness of the cosmic signs.

Guidance from the verses:

1. Warning against the punishments that follow from polytheism and sins.
2. Affirmation of the doctrine of the Last Resurrection.
3. The call to God is an obligation upon every believer who follows the Messenger ﷺ.
4. Certain knowledge is required of the one who calls to God, for it is the insight mentioned in the verse.
5. The obligation to affirm God's oneness in His divinity, lordship, names and attributes.
6. Prophethood is a distinction of men; there is no female prophet among women.
7. Clarification of the fruits of monotheism and piety in this world and the next.

2. Affirmation of the doctrine of the Last Resurrection.

6. Prophethood is a distinction of men; there is no female prophet among women.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 12, verses 107–109:

Explanation of the words:

*Ghashiyah min 'adhab Allah* (an overwhelming [calamity] from the punishment of God): i.e., a vengeance from His vengeance that overtakes them, meaning it encompasses them.

*Baghtah* (suddenly): all of a sudden, while they remain upon their polytheism and disbelief.

*Hadhihi sabili* (this is my way): i.e., my call and my method, which I follow.

*'Ala basirah* (with insight): i.e., with certain knowledge on my part.

*Wa subhan Allah* (and glory be to God): i.e., exalting God and sanctifying Him above having any partner in His dominion or any deity besides Him.

*Min ahl al-qura* (from the people of the towns): from the people of cities and metropolises, not from the people of the desert.

*Lilladhina ittaqaw* (for those who have taken God as their protection): i.e., God, by performing His obligations and abandoning His prohibitions.

*Afala ta'qilun* (will you not reason?): i.e., will these polytheists not reason about this which is recited to them and explained to them, so that they believe and affirm God's oneness.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues with the call to faith in divine revelation, to monotheism, to the Resurrection and to recompense, which are the great pillars of religion. God says: ﴿And most of them do not believe in God except that they associate others with Him﴾ [Yusuf: 106], and those who pass by many of the signs of God while turning away from them. Are these people then safe from ﴿that there should come upon them an overwhelming [calamity] from the punishment of God﴾, i.e., a punishment that envelops them and covers them with torment that cannot be withstood, ﴿or that the Hour should come upon them suddenly﴾, i.e., the Resurrection, ﴿while they are unaware﴾ of the time of its coming, so that the affliction is greatly magnified and the calamity becomes severe for them. And how can they feel safe, when is there anyone who can grant them safety other than God, the Exalted? Then what is wrong with them that they do not believe and do not fear, so that they might be saved from what is expected for them? This is what the first verse [107] indicates. As for the second, God commanded His Messenger to persist in his call, the call to good, he and the believers with him, saying: ﴿Say: This is my way﴾, i.e., say, O Messenger, to the people: this is my method in calling to my Lord, that He be believed in and worshipped alone, without any other. ﴿I call to God with insight﴾, i.e., with certain knowledge of whom I call to, of what I call with, and of the results that follow from this call, ﴿I and whoever follows me﴾ among the believers; we all call to God with insight.

And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And glory be to God﴾, i.e., say, "Glory be to God," meaning exalting Him above having any partner or son, and say likewise, declaring your innocence of polytheism and the polytheists: ﴿And I am not of the polytheists﴾. This is what the second verse indicates. As for the third verse, God informs His Messenger that He did not send before him any of the messengers, who were many, except men, i.e., not women and not angels, ﴿to whom We revealed from among the people of the towns﴾, i.e., the cities and metropolises. This is a refutation of their denial that the Messenger could be a man from among mankind. And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Have they not travelled through the land﴾, i.e., these deniers from Quraysh and others, ﴿so that they might look﴾ for lessons, ﴿and see how was the end of those before them, such as 'Ad and Thamud?﴾ For We destroyed them and saved those among them who were people of faith and monotheism, together with their messengers. This salvation is a fruit of faith and piety. ﴿And the Hereafter's abode is better for those who have taken God as their protection﴾, for it is the abode of lasting bliss and freedom from pains, afflictions, defects, senility, death and annihilation.

And His saying at the end of the verse, ﴿Will you not reason?﴾ rebukes those polytheists who insist on denial and association for their failure to reason and to understand what is recited to them, what they hear of the Qur'anic verses, and what they witness of the cosmic signs.

1. Warning against the punishments that follow from polytheism and sins.
2. Affirmation of the doctrine of the Last Resurrection.
3. The call to God is an obligation upon every believer who follows the Messenger ﷺ.
4. Certain knowledge is required of the one who calls to God, for it is the insight mentioned in the verse.
5. The obligation to affirm God's oneness in His divinity, lordship, names and attributes.
6. Prophethood is a distinction of men; there is no female prophet among women.
7. Clarification of the fruits of monotheism and piety in this world and the next.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 12, verses 110–111:

Explanation of the words:

Istay'asa al-rusul (ٱسْتَيْأَسَ ٱلرُّسُلُ): that is, they despaired of their people's faith.

Wa-zannu annahum qad kudhibu (وَظَنُّوا أَنَّهُمْ قَدْ كُذِبُوا): that is, the nations to whom the messengers were sent thought that the messengers had failed to fulfil what they had been promised of victory.

Wa-la yuraddu ba's-una (وَلَا يُرَدُّ بَأْسُنَا): that is, Our severe punishment.

'An al-qawm al-mujrimin (عَنِ ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ): that is, those who committed crimes against themselves through polytheism and sins, and committed crimes against others by turning them away from faith.

Laqad kana fi qasasihim (لَقَدْ كَانَ فِي قَصَصِهِمْ): that is, of the messengers, peace be upon them.

Ma kana hadithan yuftara (مَا كَانَ حَدِيثًا يُفْتَرَىٰ): that is, this Qur'an was not a fabricated narrative.

Tasdiq alladhi bayna yadayh (تَصْدِيقَ ٱلَّذِي بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ): that is, it confirms the divine scriptures that came before it, since it was revealed confirming them in faith and monotheism.

Meaning of the two verses:

The context continues the call to faith and monotheism through the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَا﴾ [Yusuf: 109]. That is, the messengers whom We sent continued calling to Us and persisted in their call, and their victory was delayed until despair crept into their hearts and their followers thought that they had failed to fulfil what they had been promised of victory over them and the destruction of their enemies. ﴿جَآءَهُمْ﴾ after despair had set in, Our victory came, ﴿فَنُجِّيَ مَن نَّشَآءُ ولا يُرَدُّ بَأْسُنا عَنِ ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾ [so whomever We willed was delivered, and Our punishment is not averted from the criminal people]. This is what came in the first verse: ﴿حَتّىٰ إذا ٱسْتَيْأَسَ ٱلرُّسُلُ وظَنُّوۤاْ أنَّهُمْ قَدْ كُذِبُواْ جَآءَهُمْ نَصْرُنا فَنُجِّيَ مَن نَّشَآءُ ولا يُرَدُّ بَأْسُنا عَنِ ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾ [until, when the messengers despaired and thought that they had been denied, Our victory came to them, and whomever We willed was delivered, and Our punishment is not averted from the criminal people], and they are the people of polytheism and sins.

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿لَقَدْ كانَ فِي قَصَصِهِمْ عِبْرَةٌ لأُوْلِي ٱلأَلْبابِ﴾ [There was certainly in their stories a lesson for people of understanding], that is, in the stories of the messengers with their peoples, through recounting their reports and clarifying their circumstances, from the deliverance of the believers and the destruction of the disbelieving deniers, there is a lesson by which believers take heed, so they remain steadfast in their faith and persist in their piety towards their Lord by performing His obligations and avoiding His prohibitions.

Ulu al-albab (أُولُو ٱلْأَلْبَابِ) are the people of intellect. As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿ما كانَ حَدِيثاً يُفْتَرىٰ﴾ [It was not a narrative that could be invented], that is, this mighty Qur'an is not a narrative of the kind that a human being could possibly lie about and fabricate the like of, under any circumstances. Rather, it, the Qur'an, is ﴿تَصْدِيقَ ٱلَّذِي بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ﴾ [a confirmation of what came before it], that is, what was sent down before it, such as the Torah and the Gospel. It confirms them in the fundamentals of faith and monotheism and does not contradict them. This is the greatest proof that it is a divine revelation like them, and not a fabricated speech as the falsifiers claim. As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وتَفْصِيلَ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وهُدًى ورَحْمَةً لِّقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ [and a detailing of all things, and a guidance and a mercy for a people who believe], that is, just as it confirms what is before it, it also details every matter that mankind needs in its religion, which purifies its souls, brings upon them the mercy of their Lord and His pleasure with them, and is a guidance that illuminates the path, guiding out of error, and a mercy attained by those who believe in it, act upon it, and apply its laws and rulings.

Lessons from the verses:

From the lessons of the verses:

1. The explanation of Allah's custom of delaying victory for His messengers and His believing servants, as an increase in preparation and testing; then Allah's victory comes, honouring the friends of Allah and humiliating His enemies.

2. The condemnation of criminality, which is corruption of beliefs, morals, laws and rulings.

3. The explanation of the excellence of the Qur'an and what it contains of guidance and mercy for whoever seeks them from it.

4. Believers, in that they are alive, are the ones who benefit from the guidance and mercy of the Qur'an.
